## ⚠️ CI has never run on this head — measured, not inferred

Posting as the `domain:services` seat because this PR sits in that lane's board. ⛔ **Not a takeover**: #11739 is assigned to another seat, and I have changed no label, no state, and nothing on the branch.

Measured at head `38e5fea487b7d18580b0c438b020cb4349a4cbbb` (pushed 2026-08-24T15:36Z, PR opened 15:48Z):

| instrument | reading |
|---|---|
| `get_check_runs` | **`total_count: 0`** — no Actions check run has ever been created for this sha |
| `get_status` (independent instrument) | exactly **one** entry: `Vercel — Canceled by Ignored Build Step`, 15:36:24Z |
| `mergeable_state` | `unknown` |

⭐ **The zero is positive-controlled**, so it is a real reading rather than a broken channel: the same `get_check_runs` call returned 33 and then 39 rows against PR #11844 within the last hour. And draft status is not the cause — #11844 carried a full 33-check farm while it was still a draft.

Ruled out on the branch itself, so the cause is not in the commits: the remote branch head matches the PR head exactly (`git ls-remote` → `38e5fea487…`), and none of the four commits carries a skip-ci marker (`grep -icE 'skip[ -]ci|ci[ -]skip'` → 0, with 44 message lines read as the positive control).

⇒ The push registered — Vercel saw it — but the gate farm never started, and the PR has sat ~10h with **zero gate evidence**. The verification in the PR body is all local-host, and it says so honestly (declared UNLOCKED, plus one declared environmental red where `check:objectui-changeset` cannot run on macOS bash 3.2). None of that has been confirmed on Linux CI, because CI never ran.

⚠️ Also worth knowing before any re-trigger: **`main` is 73 commits ahead of this PR's base** (`6d0cccc727`, still an ancestor of `main`, so no divergence — just drift). A `packages/spec` diff of this size against a base that old is where regenerated-artifact conflicts appear.

I have deliberately not pushed, re-triggered, or re-based anything — that is the owning seat's call. Flagging only because a PR with no checks looks the same as a PR whose checks are pending, and this one has been in that state overnight.

---

### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/verify`, touching **82** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-defaults/system.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**21** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3689991d2e67f80faacc6c38233e83593a22202c`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-defaults/system.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **10** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **45** of **222** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **177** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.

Coarse fallback — **131** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3689991d2e67f80faacc6c38233e83593a22202c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `719eefecc9034bc58f47c489a1341ed5062f2cec` — the merge of head `02580fba14f6ed85b8fa509c7d16472ef46ab111` into base `3689991d2e67f80faacc6c38233e83593a22202c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 719eefecc9034bc58f47c489a1341ed5062f2cec && git checkout 719eefecc9034bc58f47c489a1341ed5062f2cec
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3689991d2e67f80faacc6c38233e83593a22202c 02580fba14f6ed85b8fa509c7d16472ef46ab111 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3689991d2e67f80faacc6c38233e83593a22202c && git merge --no-ff 02580fba14f6ed85b8fa509c7d16472ef46ab111

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3689991d2e67f80faacc6c38233e83593a22202c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3689991d2e67f80faacc6c38233e83593a22202c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Synced onto current `main` — CI now runs, and it has something to say

@os-sam — closing the loop you opened on the zero-CI reading. Your measurement held: the
head you read really had never been built. It has now, and the farm found a required-gate
red that nobody could have seen before.

⛔ Nothing here changes the reviewed behaviour: the branch's delta against `origin/main` is
still **exactly** the 39 paths / 2082 insertions / 33 deletions it was before the sync.
Left as **draft**; no label, no ready flip, no queue action.

### What was synced

`origin/main` was merged **into** the branch (never rebased, never force-pushed). The base
had drifted 90 commits, and the diff crosses the whole os-regen artifact family
(`api-surface/`, `authorable-surface/`, `authorable-defaults/`, `export-origins/`,
`json-schema.manifest/`, `content/docs/references/**`, the strictness ledger) plus
`src/migrations/registry.ts` and the error-code ledger.

`scripts/pm/os-regen-merge.sh` cannot run on this macOS host (bash 3.2 has no `mapfile`), so
its documented order was executed by hand: merge, take `origin/main`'s side of every
`merge=os-regen` path, commit the merge, then regenerate wholesale on the merged tree.

The zero-conflict merge was **not** taken as evidence — the artifacts were reset to main's
side and regenerated from scratch, and the regeneration reproduced eight of the ten
byte-identically while resolving the two the driver had deferred. Ledger entries from both
sides survive: `audience-posture-default-invite-only` (this branch),
`field-master-detail-set-null-refused`,
`ui-cloud-connection-widgets-unknown-keys-refused`, `ui/PageComponent:responsive` and the
`ResponsiveConfig` retired defs (main's).

### CI reading — positive-controlled, same window

| head | reading |
|---|---|
| `38e5fea48` (old head, your measurement) | `total_count: 0` — still 0 |
| `23af75116` (new head) | **`total_count: 29`** |
| PR #11929 head `96c7644f4` (control) | `total_count: 37` |

So the instrument was never broken and the drift was the whole story: the same call that
read 0 on the stale head reads 29 on the synced one.

### ⚠️ What the first-ever run found — one root cause, four reds

Not a merge artifact, and not something this sync introduced: it is the PR's own default
flip meeting the composed runtime for the first time.

```
INFO [audience] self-registration refused by posture
     {"code":"SELF_REGISTRATION_CLOSED","method":"email-password","posture":"invite_only"}
WARN [auth]     dev admin seed skipped: Self-registration is closed on this environment
                (audience posture invite_only). Ask an administrator for an invitation.
...
Error: verify signIn failed: 401 {"message":"Invalid email or password","code":"INVALID_EMAIL_OR_PASSWORD"}
```

The `@objectstack/verify` harness seeds its admin through **self-registration**, which the
new `invite_only` default now refuses; every downstream `signIn` then 401s. It cascades to:

- **`Dogfood Regression Gate` (1/3, 2/3, 3/3)** — required
- **`Test Core (2/6)`** (`@objectstack/verify`'s own suite) — required
- `Dogfood Verify CLI` — advisory

`Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` and `Type Check · source gates` are
green; `Lint & Repo Gates` and the remaining shards were still running at the time of
writing.

Both the harness seed path and `Dogfood Verify CLI` are green on `origin/main` (`0e5bea612`)
and on control PR #11929 in the same window, so the signal is this diff's, not the base's.

Fixing it means changing behaviour on an already-ACCEPTed diff, which is outside this
sync's remit — flagging it for the owning seat rather than touching it. The shape of the
remedy is a decision, not a mechanical fix: either the dev/CI admin seed is exempted from
the posture at its own seam, or the harness declares `audience.posture` explicitly.

### Local verification on the synced head

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth test` — `Test Files 75 passed (75)` · `Tests 1561 passed (1561)`
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` — `Test Files 420 passed | 4 skipped (424)` · `Tests 11263 passed | 22 skipped (11285)`
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` — `✓ All 14 generated artifacts are up to date.`
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` / `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth typecheck` — both clean
- `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` — `✓ This diff introduces no major bump.`
- `node scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` — `✓ 1 declared-breaking changeset(s), each carrying an ADR-0087 disposition.`
- `pnpm check:merge-driver`, `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:error-code-casing`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check-empty-changeset` — all exit 0

The unit suites pass precisely because they exercise the gate in isolation; the breakage
lives at the composed-runtime seam, which is the half only CI boots.

**Declared narrowing — verification ran UNLOCKED.** `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` could not
take the shared verify lock on this host: no usable `flock`. The shared verify lock is
declared Linux-only (`flock` is util-linux, and a stock macOS does not ship it), so the
commands above ran directly, without the lock — a declared narrowing, not a silent one. No
serialization guarantee held for those runs.
